newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Five Manila telephone firms meet line targets.
newsitem.headline: Five Manila telephone firms meet line targets.

text.p: The Philippines National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) said on Wednesday five of 10 telephone companies had installed on target their telephone line commitments as of the third quarter of this year.

NTC head Simeon Kintanar told reporters the companies were Globe Telecom, Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc, ICC Telecoms, Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and the Philippine Telephone & Telegraph.
Of the 10, only two failed to meet their line commitments namely Isla Communications Philippines Inc, a unit of Deustche Telecom and Major Telecom Inc.
Islacom was able to put up only 6 percent of its 9,332 line commitment while MajorTel installed 9 percent of its 44,002 lines promised, he said.
"We will require these two companies to do catch up programmes so they can meet their promises by year-end," said Kintanar.

The companies which have not submitted their line commitments were Pilipino Telephone Corp, Smart Communications Co Inc, and a unit of Cable & Wireless Plc, Eastern Telecommunications Philippines Inc.
The 10 companies have committed to install 886,321 lines by September 1996. Kintanar said that so far, 1.34 million lines have been installed.

Under telecommunication laws, a cellular phone company is required to lay down 400,000 lines while an international gateway facility (IGF) operator is supposed to install 300,000 lines in a three-year period.
Each of the firms were required to submit roll-out plans to the NTC with a detailed number of telephone lines to be installed on a quarterly basis.
